transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-04
Start: 16:30 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Avery Collins (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Michael Tran (BeaconPay CTO), Sara Ortiz (BeaconPay Eng Manager), Devon Park (BeaconPay Platform)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Quick hosted API demo. Covered streaming flow, param trade-offs, retries, and observability. Agreed pilot to run perf test and share pricing.

--- Transcript (selected excerpts) ---
[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Avery from Redwood. Quick round of intros — Priya's gonna run the demo, I'm here for pricing and next steps.
[00:12] Michael: Hey. Michael here, I'm the CTO at BeaconPay. We're looking at how to add a realtime chat assistant to our merchant portal.
[00:18] Sara: Sara, engineering manager — focused on production constraints, mainly latency and PCI-adjacent data handling.
[00:25] Devon: Devon, platform, I'll be doing the integration and scaling tests.
[00:33] Priya: Great, thanks. I'll share my screen for a short walkthrough of the hosted /chat endpoint — we'll do a streaming example, tweak params, then show a retry pattern and what you see in the Console.
[01:05] Priya: Ok starting with basic call shape — you POST to /v1/chat with model, messages, stream=true. Response comes back as a chunked event stream, a token at a time. You can do client-side aggregation or stream directly into UI.
[01:40] Michael: Quick Q, what's the typical token latency from your hosted nodes? We need <120ms per token for our interactive flows.
[01:52] Priya: It depends on model and sequence length. For the curated small-LLaM-ish models we show ~60-110ms median per token at 1–2 token streams, but at high concurrency that can go up. We also have auto-batching and prefix KV cache to drop the tail latency.
[02:18] Sara: When you say KV cache, you mean like saved prefix key-value in the runtime? How does that work with multitenant hosted?
[02:27] Priya: Yeah, KV cache stored in the serving layer so repeated prefixes don't recompute. In hosted it's sharded per-tenant and encrypted. The transcripts sometimes shows "K V cash" in auto-text but it's K V cache — sorry for the tts artifacts.
[02:45] Devon: For PCI-sensitive flows we probably need to avoid sending raw card data. Is there a recommended pattern for redaction or client-side tokenization?
[02:54] Avery: Good point. Hosted supports customer-managed redact rules at the ingest layer and you can request no data retention; we also integrate with KMS for key control. We'll put the security brief in the follow up.
[03:10] Priya: Back to streaming: demo time. I'm sending a prompt: "Help an SMB reconcile a refund request — give step-by-step."
[03:25] [Priya's screen share: streams arrive token by token — visible partial sentences]
[03:40] Priya: Notice the first chunk came quick, then a small pause — that's the runtime doing attention across the growing sequence. Client can show a spinner between chunks.
[04:02] Michael: If a chunk fails mid-stream and you retry, do you recommence from start or resume?
[04:12] Priya: We recommend idempotent request IDs and client-side resume. For streaming you can do resumable session ids — Redwood's SDK returns the last emitted token index, so you can request a suffix. If you just re-POST without idempotency you'll get a full new generation and you'll need to diff.
[04:35] Michael: That idempotent id — is that something we generate or you accept an idempotency-key header?
[04:42] Priya: You supply 'x-idempotency-key' and we persist mapping for 24 hours for hosted. For longer pilots we can extend TTL.
[05:00] Sara: How do you handle 429 vs 5xx from the runtime? Our load tests often spike and then backoff.
[05:08] Priya: For 429 we suggest an exponential backoff with jitter starting at 200ms, doubling with cap ~8s. For transient 5xx, slightly longer initial backoff and retry up to 3 attempts; we surface error codes in the stream trailer. For streaming specifically, do not blindly concatenate partial responses — verify via the resume token/last-index.
[05:45] Devon: Any examples for recommended retry windows?
[05:49] Priya: Sure — sample: for 429 -> wait 200ms, 500ms, 1s; for 5xx -> 500ms, 1.5s, 3s. Jitter +-20%. We'll put code in the follow-up guide.
[06:12] [timestamp drift in transcription; speaker sometimes listed as Speaker 1 for a short bit]
[07:00] Priya: Now parameter tuning: temperature, top_p, frequency_penalty, presence_penalty, max_tokens. Use temperature 0.0–0.3 for deterministic outputs — good for transactional messages. For creative help center copy maybe 0.6–0.9. Top_p as complement.
[07:35] Michael: We're worried about hallucinations in refunds flow, need deterministic and auditable outputs.
[07:42] Priya: For that use low temperature, include system prompt with strict instructions and stop sequences. Also run a small reranker post-gen if you want absolute guardrails — Redwood supports a reranking step in the pipeline.
[08:05] Sara: Does reranking add latency?
[08:09] Priya: Yes small additional latency — depends on number of candidates. You can instead run a light classification filter inline which is quicker.
[08:22] Michael: Could you show a quick example with stop sequences?
[08:28] Priya: Sure — sending a chat with stop: ["

"]. You can also set max_tokens low for short bullet answers.
[09:05] [Demo: toggles max_tokens and temperature — partial outputs change accordingly]
[09:40] Devon: On cost — streaming vs non-streaming, do you bill per-token as they stream or per final?
[09:48] Avery: We bill per output token for hosted regardless of streaming, plus input tokens. Streaming doesn't change the unit of billing, just how it's delivered. The Console shows token breakdown per-route so you can see it in near-real-time.
[10:10] Michael: Is the console able to show per-request token trail? We want to associate a token cost to a user session id.
[10:20] Priya: Yes, you can pass a metadata field per request (client_session_id) and Console traces allow filtering by tag, then you can export a CSV of token counts.
[10:38] Sara: Security: SSO and audit logs — do you have SAML/SSO and fine-grained RBAC?
[10:46] Avery: Yes SSO via SAML and OIDC, SCIM for provisioning, and RBAC with role granularity. Audit logs include per-route request/response metadata — payload logging is opt-in and can be disabled.
[11:10] Michael: Data residency — our regulators prefer EU-only storage. Is hosted available in region X?
[11:18] Avery: We have EU-hosted regions; you can also use Redwood Private for strict on-prem or VPC-only deployment. For hosted, we can pin in eu-west-1 region and apply retention policies.
[11:36] Priya: Back to demo — now showing Console: trace view shows start time, per-token latency histogram, and the model variant used. We can drill into a request and see the stream chunks appended and the trailer code.
[12:05] [screen: Console trace example, table of tokens and timings]
[12:45] Michael: Any mechanism for automatic fallback if a particular model is overloaded?
[12:51] Priya: Yes, smart routing policies. You can configure fallback model families — Redwood will route to a compatible smaller variant automatically if the primary is saturated, subject to your SLO preferences. That keeps the app online with degraded quality instead of errors.
[13:18] Sara: For A/B comparatives we want canary rollout — is that in the Console?
[13:25] Avery: Yep canary and A/B deploys are supported, with percent-based traffic split and metrics to compare latency/cost/quality.
[13:40] Devon: How do we capture partial transcripts for audit? If streaming is interrupted, we want a durable transcript.
[13:48] Priya: The SDK can append chunks to a durable store or you can request the final transcript from the server by referencing the session id — there's a replay API. For legal reasons you can also store only the redacted metadata.
[14:12] Michael: Could you talk about throttling — at what point will hosted throttle us?
[14:20] Avery: Hosted enforces per-account QPS and token-per-minute quotas. For pilots we'll provision generous soft limits, and we can increase after observing your profile. If you hit quotas, Console shows the exception type and a sample id you can contact support with.
[14:40] Sara: Are there SDKs we should use for streaming? We prefer node and python.
[14:46] Priya: Yes official SDKs for Node and Python, plus a lightweight REST example. The SDKs handle parsing the chunked stream and expose resume tokens and the last-index. We'll share those snippets.
[15:10] [Minor crosstalk — brief network glitch noted by Devon]
[16:05] Priya: Now a failure-mode demo: I'll simulate a transient 503 in the middle of a stream and show how client can resume using idempotency-key and last-index.
[16:22] [Simulated 503 mid-stream; console shows "stream-trailer: transient_error code=503" ]
[16:45] Priya: On the client we catch that, call the resume endpoint with session id and start_index=last_emitted+1 — server will return the suffix tokens.
[17:05] Michael: If we accidentally duplicate some tokens when resuming, how do you suggest dedupe?
[17:12] Priya: Track last confirmed index and only append tokens with index > last. Also server returns hash of previous chunk for verification. Small inconsistencies can occur with partial transcripts but resumable ids minimize deltas.
[17:40] Sara: Does using resume require storing state server-side?
[17:48] Priya: We store resume pointers for a TTL (24h default). For longer we can extend. For Dedicated you can have different retention.
[18:05] Devon: We want to test 1k concurrent sessions, any guidance?
[18:12] Avery: For that scale, Dedicated or reserved capacity is recommended to guarantee throughput. Hosted can burst but sustained high QPS is better done on Dedicated. We'll provide a capacity planning doc.
[18:28] Michael: What's the rough cost delta moving from hosted to Dedicated?
[18:34] Avery: Dedicated is committed pricing — lower unit cost but with a monthly commitment. For small pilots we usually start hosted; if sustained QPS beyond X, we estimate Dedicated becomes cheaper. I'll include example math.
[18:55] [15-minute demo continues — skipping some blocks in this transcript for brevity]
[34:10] Priya: Quick note on safety filters — we can run built-in content policy checks inline; they return block/flag actions and don't add much latency.
[34:35] Sara: Can those policies be tuned per-tenant?
[34:38] Priya: Yes you can override on a per-route basis.
[35:00] Michael: Any known migrations challenges from other vendors? We used a different vendor internally before — OpenAI-ish.
[35:10] Avery: Main differences are auth model and metadata tags. We map fields and offer helpers to translate. Also we do more routing controls and observability out of the box.
[36:00] Sara: For our compliance team, can you provide SOC2 and encryption documentation?
[36:05] Avery: Yes, we'll attach SOC 2 Type II, and KMS/HSM integration docs in the follow-up.
[36:30] Devon: Lastly, what's the SLA on hosted?
[36:35] Avery: Hosted has an uptime objective but enterprise SLA is part of Dedicated contracts. Hosted is best-effort with incident notifications; Dedicated has formal SLAs.
[37:05] [short break while Priya runs a longer sample]
[42:20] Priya: Running a longer multi-turn chat to show prefix caching: first run is slower, second with same prefix is faster due to KV cache. See the per-token latency drop in Console.
[43:00] Michael: That looks compelling. If we seed the same system prompt across sessions will that be shared?
[43:08] Priya: The cache is per-tenant and per-prefix hash. Shared system prompts produce cache hits if identical. If you vary anything it invalidates the cache.
[43:35] Sara: We'll need to normalize prompts for caching to be effective.
[43:40] Devon: Do you provide tooling to fingerprint prompts?
[43:43] Priya: There's a prompt hashing helper in the SDK. We'll include it.
[44:05] Michael: Ok recap — main concerns: latency targets, cost, and security/audit.
[44:15] Avery: Recap from Redwood side: (1) we'll send pricing spreadsheet and capacity planning; (2) Priya will share streaming & retry code snippets and Console walkthrough recording; (3) BeaconPay runs 24h perf run and posts sample traces; (4) we'll reconvene after they have data.
[44:38] Sara: Sounds good. Also we want a short doc on recommended param presets for transactional vs creative flows.
[44:45] Priya: We'll add a one-page cheat sheet with presets.
[45:05] Michael: Any blockers for starting a small pilot this week?
[45:10] Avery: Only an account setup and billing card — we can spin up pilot credentials same day after you accept the terms.
[45:22] Devon: I'll send our peak QPS numbers and a sample payload schema.
[45:28] Michael: Ok schedule follow-up for the week of 8/23.
[45:35] Avery: I'll send calendar invites and share the resources. Thanks everyone.
[45:40] Sara: Thanks!
[45:42] Michael: Thanks, bye.
[45:44] [call end]
